shouldFix.title: The field that states this artifact's own condition-4 recording effect is inherited unchanged, disclaimed as dated, and says the opposite of the live standing — so the artifact answers that question wrongly rather than declining to answer it
shouldFix.finding: condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded is byte-identical to v4 and v3. It says a later recording 'would move condition 4's harness half from 0 of 18 required names toward 16 of 18', that 'G03/G04 remain required and unnamed until a D-006-conforming successor', and that 'Condition 4 would still not be MET: two required gates (G03/G04) remain unnamed'. Live file 08 says condition 4 is MET, with 18 of 18 required gates naming a recorded identifier and G03/G04 named under D-102. v5 handles this by listing the field in inheritedRecitals as DATED-D086-ERA with liveStanding governing, which is honest and is why this is not a blocker. But this field is not a historical recital like the G03/G04 namingStanding values — it is the artifact's statement of what recording *this artifact* would do, and this artifact is awaiting exactly that recording. After the disclaimer, the artifact contains no live answer to its own question. The true answer is simple, in scope, and better than a disclaimer: recording v5 has zero condition-4 naming effect, because DR-G20 and DR-G21 are both already in requiredNow and both already carry namingStanding NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, so no new identifier is named and no denominator moves. I verified each of those four facts. The hazard is concrete: every recording entry in this corpus states a readiness effect, and a coordinator drafting that entry would find this artifact's own field predicting a 0-to-16-of-18 movement and condition 4 not MET, which is the opposite of the live standing.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing is asserted without a disclaimer. inheritedRecitals names the field explicitly and says liveStanding governs, and liveStanding is accurate, so a careful reader is not misled. The defect is that the artifact leaves the recorder to derive an answer it could state in one sentence.
shouldFix.repair: Add one sentence to liveStanding, or a short thisSuccessorCondition4Effect field: recording this successor names no new identifier — DR-G20 and DR-G21 are already in the 18 and already NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED — so its condition-4 effect is zero and condition 4 stays MET on the naming half and below QUALIFIED. Leave condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded inherited and dated as it is; rewriting v3's arithmetic is properly a different act.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Thirteen attacks run, one landed. Custody is clean: c2dad453 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 1ac85c7, both predecessors frozen, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree. My v4 finding lands in full and in its durable form: COORD is re-measured to the live e838775b, HEAD is pinned, all five file pins now reproduce, and remeasurementClause gained the PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT limb I recommended over a bare re-measure. My v4 advisory is resolved too, since the sentence that dangled was dropped with the clause rewrite. The other reviewer's stale-recital finding I checked independently rather than on the disposition table, and the fix is accurate: the v3-era G03/G04 standing really is dated, D-102 named those identifiers at dual CONSENT, and liveStanding's quoted condition-4 lead is a byte-exact prefix of live file 08's measured cell, with 'MET for the naming/owner half … Not QUALIFIED' mapping precisely onto that row's criterion of named harnesses and owners plus no unevidenced QUALIFIED. I also tested the enumeration for completeness by auditing all 22 namingStanding values: G13 and G17 are the only other non-standard ones, and neither is stale, because neither sits in requiredNow. All 22 gate entries are byte-identical to v4, so the DR-133 naming I checked last cycle is preserved intact and nothing crept in elsewhere, and nothing was deleted to pay for a repair. What blocks is one field. condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded states what recording this artifact would do to condition 4 — it says the move is toward 16 of 18 and that condition 4 would still not be MET — and it is inherited unchanged while live file 08 says condition 4 is MET at 18 of 18. v5 handles it by listing the field as DATED-D086-ERA with liveStanding governing, which is honest and is why it is not a blocker; but this is not a historical recital, it is the artifact's answer to the question its own recording will pose, and after the disclaimer there is no live answer. The true answer is one sentence and I verified it: recording v5 names no new identifier, because DR-G20 and DR-G21 are already in the 18 and already NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, so the condition-4 effect is zero. A coordinator drafting the recording entry must state a readiness effect and would otherwise find this artifact predicting the opposite of the live standing. Three items I considered and declined are recorded so the choices are auditable.
